newsitem.title: INDONESIA: SembCorp sees S$30 mln sale from Karimun.
newsitem.headline: SembCorp sees S$30 mln sale from Karimun.

text.p: Sembawang Shipyard, a unit of Sembawang Corp, said on Monday it expects total sales of between $20 million and $30 million in 1997 from its two new facilities on Karimun Island.
"We are expecting total sales of between $20 and $30 million in 1997," Heng Chiang Gnee, managing director of Sembawang Shipyard, told reporters.
He was speaking after the official opening of the Karimum Marine and Industrial Complex (KMIC) and PT. Karimun Sembawang Shipyard (PT KSS) on Indonesia's Karimun Island.
The complex was opened by Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and Indonesian President Soeharto.

KMIC is an integrated industrial facility for marine and engineering firms developed by PT. Karimun Indojaya Corporation, a consortium comprising Indonesia's Salim Group, Sembawang Corp and Singapore's JTC (Jurong Town Corporation) International.
PT KSS is a 65:35 percent joint venture between Sembawang Shipyard and the Salim Group.

Lai Chun Loong, president of Sembawang Industrial, which manages the development of KMIC, said he expected the construction of the second phase of KMIC, costing around Singapore $200 million, to begin in 1999.
Sembawang Corp said in a statement that phase two, covering 260 hectares, would include an additional 400-meter pier and a larger floating dock.
"The first phase encompassing 155 hectares at an estimated costs of S$90 million are already in place," it said.
Lai said Sembawang could relocate its ship repair facilities from Singapore to Karimun.
He said discussions were also under way with Asian companies on a dozen projects for both facilities. He gave no details.
"Karimun embodies the expansionistic move by SembCorp to regionalise the group's ship repair business," the Sembawang statement said.
